there was no time in the city, she mused, as she put her poker table in order for the evening. The year, date and even time of day had no effect on things, because las vegas would always be clanging coins, flipping cards, slot machines churning noise, and the money. Always the perpetually flowing money. Elaine's skill as a poker dealer, and her sharp eye had gotten her many promotions over the years, and she was proud to have her own table to manage in a small, sealed room inside the casino, all to itself, and herself.

When the value in a game was expected to go over certain amounts, holding it out on the noise of the main floor was begging for theft, and so rooms like this existed. A billion dollars could easily pass by in this room, as simply as a light bet, and as cheap as throwing a single bottom poker chip in. the money would always be here to play cards, they might be odd, strange, or from some obscure part of the world, so tonight’s scheduled player were unlikely to faze her. She glanced at the clock, sliding stacks of chips into neat place. Ten minutes to go. Someone though, popped in the door early.

It was the one who had scheduled the room, elaine saw.

A tall, bone thin young man with pale skin, long black hair, and a green glint to his eye. His suit was a deep dark green, like moss in moonlit shadow. She folded her hands behind her back and said “mr.key”. She hadnt ever spoken to this man, but she had heard stories, and he was a known VIP. “it a fine day for tricks, get me a bottle of ale here” he said, loosening his tie, throwing it to the table. Had it bounced too much, and moved a bit after it settled? or had her eyes deceived her. She set her mind back to her job, and grabbed the bottle of brown liquid from a bar fridge under the table.

Security measures here weren't extensive, as privacy was important to anyone rich enough to be here, but she did have some cameras wired to small screens, just out of view, mounted at an angle where the players were none the wiser. Glancing down as she straightened, she saw on one view a bugs eye view right below, from a small glass dot in the carpet at her feet. Here she could see the the players feet, and underside of the table. If someone hid cards down there, she’d be able to tell. The second small screen was a camera mounted invincibly in a corner of the ceiling, a little glass bead set in the eye of a decorative stone cherub, who held up the ceiling, with three of his friends in the other corners.

A birds eye view. In both views elaine saw mr.key, and assigned him to a spot in a mental map that was forming in her head, rough boundaries that any funny business would alert her to. Two more players were expected. She idly chatted “so, a quick game today?”. She took out her own ale bottle, and sipped at it. Legally she wasn't supposed to drink on the job, but her room, her poker table, her rules, and damn what anyone else said. This was when you talked to the players anyways, got a sense of each of their baselines. mr.key smiled and said “it might be quick, but sometimes heavy matters are best settled by a card game. Big players tonight”.

He wet a finger in the ale at the moth of the bottle, and muttered something under his breath as he drew a soaked design into the felt. Something with straight lines, like a tree with two rows of branches, but one half sheared off. He looked up and smiled “let’s hope no one cheats today”. She returned the smile, bitter, sipping ale. It was always the ones who mentioned cheating first she mused. But, there was no reason to suspect him yet, and at this paygrade, it might be safer to let him cheat. The door swung open, and a tall, thin african man who smiled like the sunlight entered. He boomed in a thick African accent “and I ‘ear you want to play cards, you dirty trickster”. It wasn't an insult, it was a greeting. He swooped into his seat, and mr.key raised his glass to him, “player number three is who we’ll both be glad to see”. “yes” the tall african boomed, agreeing. To Elaine, he extended a hand, shaking it and saying “call me mr.ansi, miss” she blushed, holding the shake. Before he let go he asked “do you mind if I invite a friend to watch?”. Elaine nodded yes to that. As she broke the shake, he kept his hand extended, but held it up palm facing up.

A spider crawled out his sleeve, as large as a tarantula but as black and skinny as a black widow. It obediently sat in his hand, and when he set it on the tables edge, it crouched, intently observing with too much intelligence for a spider to rightly have. She resisted the urge to scream, and said “its a cute friend” through a choked voice. The African man boomed a laugh and said “ayy, but it is. This one evaded a man in south america by scurrying onto his back, and not moving while he searched. I like his way of thinking”. Throught out this whole exchange,m he gestured at the spider, which crouched, stared at her, and idly rubbed mandibles so large they were visible.

With all the backbone she could muster, she did not freak out at this sight, instead sipping ale and saying “that's very interesting, but make sure he doesn't interfere with the poker game”. she’d seen a lot of weird shit working in las vegas, but this was already at the boundary and the money, and the cards hadnt even started flying yet. “he will not, madam. There are times for jokes, and then they are times with rules” he said gravely. The clock ticked to the scheduled time. She turned the two and said “so where the third then?”. A cold feeling passed through the room, and the small amount of ale remaining in her bottle froze, dropping the temperature of her glass to frostbite levels. One single puff of her breath came out as steam. Suddenly, the cold wasn't there anymore.

“on time, and here” said a deep male voice from one of the seats. As she put down her frozen bottle, she found a man sitting in the third seat. His suit was a black as death, his skin was white as bone, and his black hair and beard had the loose tumble of a warrior fresh from battle. He turned to regard mr.key and coldly stated “i do this as a gesture of diplomacy. The sooner ive unraveled the plan you two have for me, I’ll flip this table and leave, and get back to work”. The third mans voice had something ominious in its tone, like half the sound wasnt even in this reality. “and you are?” elaine asked. “hades” the man said simply, not shaking her hand, “let us play this game, then”.

“thats a distinctive name” she chatted, pulling out a card boot.
